schema: Lab catalogue research brief v1 shape, plus the extensions listed in conventions.extensions
status: PROPOSAL - nothing here is signed. Ranges import as unsigned drafts; concepts and tests import as an addendum for sign-off.

conventions.age: Age at collection in days. ageFromDays inclusive, ageToDays exclusive, null = open (Phase 1 RR-4). Years converted as floor(years x 365.25), months as floor(months x 30.4375).
conventions.units: UCUM. Each concept has one canonical unit; otherUnits are accepted at entry only where multiplyBy is a plain factor. Affine conversions carry a formula and are display-only.
conventions.flags: No critical limits are proposed anywhere in this file.

extensions.range.kind: reference (population interval; drives H/L) | decision (clinical decision limit or category scheme; drives interpretation)
extensions.band.label / band.scheme / band.context: decision categories, the guideline they come from, the clinical state they apply to, which side of the limit is inclusive, and age-dependent limits
extensions.band.strand / range.strands / concept.st: which research strand produced it (A1-A7), for audit
extensions.band.verification: an open verification problem; the band must not be signed until it is cleared
extensions.concept.answers[]: objects {code, display, abnormal, approxValue?} rather than strings; abnormal drives the abnormal marker for coded results
extensions.concept.loincAlternatives: other verified LOINC terms for other units, specimens or methods

otherUnits.formula: IFCC (mmol/mol) = (10.93 x NGSP%) - 23.50 ; inverse master equation: NGSP% = (0.09148 x IFCC) + 2.152

formulaSource.citation: NGSP. IFCC Standardization: IFCC and NGSP.
formulaSource.where: Master equation text and Table 2 (NGSP designated comparison method)

otherUnits.notes: The NGSP page states the master equation as NGSP = 0.09148*IFCC + 2.152. Its algebraic inverse, (NGSP - 2.152)/0.09148, is about 10.931*NGSP - 23.52, which is not identical to the Table 2 form (10.93*NGSP - 23.50). The difference is less than 0.1 mmol/mol, so it vanishes when IFCC is reported as an integer. Recommend implementing IFCC = (NGSP - 2.152) / 0.09148, rounded to 0 dp, so that both directions use the same equation.

concepts.notes: Use an NGSP-certified, DCCT-traceable method (ADA Table 2.1). Show mmol/mol to 0 dp. HbA1c is unreliable with haemoglobin variants (HbS/HbC; HbSS, HbCC and HbSC 'must be interpreted with caution', NGSP), shortened red-cell survival or haemolysis (falsely low), iron deficiency (higher HbA1c), pregnancy in the second and third trimesters and postpartum, recent blood loss or transfusion, erythropoietin, haemodialysis, HIV or its treatment, G6PD deficiency (ADA Rec 2.4), and malaria or other accelerated red-cell turnover (WHO 2011). Each of these is highly relevant in Uganda. The UI should carry an interpretive caveat, and the order form could capture known Hb variant or pregnancy status.

concepts.notes: Westergren is the ICSH reference method (adopted 1973, reaffirmed with CLSI 2011, per StatPearls). Raised by anaemia and pregnancy, and by age and female sex. Reported slightly higher in African-American than Caucasian populations (Gillum 1993, cited via Wikipedia). Elderly Black South Africans had much higher 99th centiles (Bester 1993).

loinc.longName: Erythrocyte [Sedimentation Rate] in Blood by Westergren method

concepts.notes: Existing concept. Proposal: retire in favour of obs.troponin_i_hs / obs.troponin_t_hs, or keep only if the hospital runs a single assay and records which. cTnI and cTnT are different analytes, and hs-cTnI values are not comparable across manufacturers. Recommend splitting into obs.troponin_t_hs and obs.troponin_i_hs, or requiring a mandatory method attribute. The 99th percentile URL is assay-specific, and sex-specific URLs are recommended for hs assays (Apple 2017).

Existing unit is mg/L; this makes the FEU basis explicit (UCUM annotation {FEU}). DDU-reporting analysers use obs.d_dimer_ddu. DECISION: the unit must carry FEU or DDU explicitly. At least 28 unit combinations are in use, with potential errors of about 2000-fold (CCLM 2020). Proposed canonical unit is ug/L FEU, with DDU kept as a distinct unit and no automatic conversion. Cut-offs are assay-specific.

tests.methodNotes: Dymind DH-615 (brochure P/N EN-DH615[3.0], https://www.amdsolutions.com.my/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/dh-615.pdf): 35 reportable parameters = the 27 CBC+DIFF parameters on the hospital report + 8 reticulocyte parameters (RET%, RET#, RHE, IRF, LFR, MFR, HFR, IPF) available in CBC+RET modes; 29 research-use-only parameters (incl. NRBC#/%, NLR, PLR, PDW-CV, Micro/Macro, HFC, IME, FRC) which must NOT be released as clinical results. Methods: WBC/RBC/PLT impedance; DIFF/RET semiconductor laser scatter + fluorescence; HGB cyanide-free colorimetric; up to 100 T/h; 20 uL CBC, 30 uL CBC+DIFF. 3-part analysers (e.g. Mindray BC-3000Plus brochure, https://www.mindray.com/content/dam/xpace/en_in/resources/brochures/bc-3000plus-product-brochure-en_in.pdf): 19 parameters - WBC, Lymph#, Mid#, Gran#, Lymph%, Mid%, Gran%, RBC, HGB, HCT, MCV, MCH, MCHC, RDW-CV, RDW-SD, PLT, MPV, PDW, PCT. Mindray BC-20s: '19 parameters + 3 histograms' (names not listed on product page). Reticulocyte parameters belong to a separate reticulocyte test (out of scope for A1).
Flow cytometry; single-platform (e.g. FACSCount) or dual-platform (uses FBC WBC and lymphocyte %). Point-of-care CD4 analysers typically report absolute count only.
Add bicarbonate (optional - many Ugandan analysers do not run it) and auto-calculated eGFR (adults only). Record creatinine method (Jaffe/enzymatic) per lab.
GGT added as optional component. Albumin method (BCG vs BCP) to be recorded.
Decision limits only (ATP III classification; ESC targets need risk category). Record fasting state and whether LDL is calculated or direct.
Random glucose; decision flag >=11.1 'diagnostic if symptomatic'.
PROPOSED: repoint from obs.glucose to new obs.glucose_fasting so WHO fasting categories apply only here.
Plasma NaF/KOx; record arterial/venous/capillary and POC vs lab.
Record hs-CRP vs standard CRP.
NGSP-certified method. Prefer an assay without Hb-variant interference (ADA, for sickle trait). Display the IFCC mmol/mol value alongside.
Thyroid function panel; FT3 is optional and reflexive. All intervals are analyser-specific, so record the platform.

Record reagent lot, ISI and MNPT with each lot change. PT reference interval and MNPT must be locally derived (MNPT: geometric mean of >=20 normal plasmas, Practical-Haemostasis). CLSI H47 3rd ed (2023) covers the PT/APTT procedure.
Proposed new test. APTT depends on activator, incubation time and automation, so the reference interval must be local.
Westergren (ICSH reference). Alternative automated methods need verification against Westergren.
Each hospital enables the one its analyser measures. Record analyte (I vs T) and assay. The lab enters its assay's 99th percentile URL, sex-specific for hs assays.
Record manufacturer and kit, unit type (FEU or DDU), and assay cut-off (CCLM 2020 minimum reporting set).
Record specimen (plasma or DBS), platform (lab or POC) and assay LoD. Support a 'not detected' result.
Spot urine ACR, preferably first-morning sample (KDIGO). Urine albumin and creatinine could be added as components if the analyser reports them; out of scope here.

10-parameter strip (Multistix 10 SG pad order: glucose, bilirubin, ketones, SG, blood, pH, protein, urobilinogen, nitrite, leukocytes; Combur-10 has the same 10 analytes). ADD bilirubin and urobilinogen to the current 8. Approximate concentrations per grade are brand-specific: record the strip product as a method attribute and keep per-brand approxValue tables. Visual read against the bottle colour chart; Downstate Lab-23G gives sensitivities.

Giemsa thick and thin film. WHO MM-SOP-08: >=100 thick-film fields before 'no malaria parasites seen'; if positive, 100 more fields for mixed infection; thin film to confirm species. MM-SOP-09: count asexual parasites against 200 WBC (if >=100 parasites) else 500 WBC; density = count x 8000 / WBC counted unless patient WBC known; thin film when >100 parasites/field. Gametocytes reported present, not counted. Species, stage, gametocytes and density visible only when result = parasites seen. Plus grade optional/legacy pending sign-off.

Record kit name, target (HRP2 Pf-only; HRP2/pLDH Pf/Pan; pLDH) and lot as method attributes; the allowed answers depend on the kit type. Faint test line = positive. No control line = invalid, repeat. pfhrp2/3 deletions (WHO 2024 response plan): HRP2-only RDTs may miss deleted parasites; WHO 5% threshold for switching.

SMI B 37: incubate 5-7 days at 35-37 C; preliminary negative ~48 h; final negative at 5 days unless extended. Positive bottle -> Gram stain phoned promptly then written. Full microbiology (organism coding, AST, contaminant rules) is Phase 4.

Serial algorithm. Uganda 2022 consolidated guidelines: Determine (screening) -> Stat-Pak (confirmatory) -> SD Bioline (tie-breaker); T1 non-reactive = negative; T1+T2 reactive = positive; T1 reactive/T2 non-reactive -> T3; T3 reactive = inconclusive, retest after 14 days; second inconclusive -> UVRI; verification retest before ART. MoH circular Nov 2024 (news report, May 2025): Wondfo One Step HIV 1/2 (A1) -> One Step Anti-HIV (A2) -> MeriScreen HIV 1/2 (A3), implementation stalled at that time. Keep kits and algorithm as versioned configuration; capture kit name and lot per test event.
IMMY CrAg LFA. Specimen qualifier: serum/plasma/whole blood/CSF. Titre only if positive and requested: 1:5 then 2-fold to >=1:2560.

Consider splitting into test.rpr, test.tpha and test.syphilis_rdt / test.dual_hiv_syphilis_rdt so each order has only its own components. A dual-RDT HIV line feeds the national HIV algorithm, never a final HIV status.
RDT or immunoassay; capture kit name/lot.
RDT or immunoassay; reactive -> HCV RNA (separate test).
Qualitative urine hCG cassette; kit sensitivity (e.g. 25 mIU/mL) is a method attribute.

Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra. RIF component shown only when MTB detected (any level); trace -> RIF indeterminate. Invalid/error/no result -> repeat on a new specimen. Trace interpretation shown as decision support (PLHIV/children/extrapulmonary = positive; adults with TB in last 5 years = culture). Specimen type is a qualifier (sputum, stool, CSF, etc.).
Determine TB LAM Ag, urine; read 25-35 min against the current (revised) Reference Scale Card; positive >= Grade 1.
WHO-IUATLD grading; scale depends on stain method (ZN x1000 vs fluorescence 200-250x). Scanty count mandatory when grade = scanty.
Forward and reverse ABO grouping; anti-D (two reagents to confirm negatives). Blood bank, antibody screen and crossmatch are Phase 4.
eGFR calculated for adults only, once the lab declares an IDMS-traceable creatinine method.

ranges.recommendation: [A1] Draft: Eller 2008 sex-specific (Ugandan, 2.5-97.5th). Note the lower limits (F 9.8, M 11.6 g/dL) are well below WHO anaemia cutoffs because healthy-population intervals include subclinical iron deficiency and Hb-variant carriers; the lab lead must decide whether the flag shown to clinicians uses the reference interval or the WHO anaemia decision limit (see decision range below). Kibaya 2008 Hb excluded: printed values (M 9.9, F 8.44) are inconsistent with g/dL and are probably mmol/L - unit not verifiable. [A2] Ugandan data (Lugada) for 1 week-18 y; Kenyan CLSI data (Kilifi) for 4 wk-17 mo as an alternative infant set. Note the Kilifi bands (e.g. 6-12 mo lower limit 7.0 g/dL) and Lugada <1 y lower limit 6.8 g/dL reflect unscreened anaemia in malaria-endemic populations - they sit well below WHO anaemia cut-offs (Hb <11.0 g/dL for 6-59 mo). Recommend the lab lead decide whether Hb flags use the local reference interval or WHO anaemia thresholds (A-strand decision); do not average the two sources.

ranges.recommendation: [A1] Use as the clinical anaemia decision layer (flag + severity grade) alongside, not instead of, the population reference interval. Verify against the WHO primary PDF before go-live. Severity labels are clinical categories, not critical limits.

source.citation: Khurana et al. 2024 Indian Pediatrics, Table III (citing Sharma et al. 2019, as adopted by WHO 2024)

altitude.rule: Amount subtracted from observed Hb or added to the anaemia cutoff (g/L); equation: Hb adjustment (g/L) = (0.0056384 x elevation) + (0.0000003 x elevation^2)

adjustments.smoking: WHO 2024 adjusts for smoking; The Blood Project (https://www.thebloodproject.com/definition-of-anemia-hb-thresholds/) reports an effect of about 6 g/L at 30 cigarettes/day; the adjustment table itself was not openable.
adjustments.ethnicity: WHO 2024 recommends against adjusting Hb cutoffs for ancestry/race/ethnicity (per The Blood Project summary of WHO 2024).

age >60 y (no source sampled beyond 59 y)
Duffy-null genotype: carriers have lower neutrophil counts without infection risk
Malaria / helminth exposure (not excluded in Lugada or Kilifi)
Sickle cell trait/disease and alpha-thalassaemia (not screened)
Analyser platform (Coulter AcT 5Diff in both main sources; MedSync sites may run Sysmex/Mindray)
Duffy-null associated (benign ethnic) neutropenia - common in East African children; explains lower neutrophil limits than Western ranges
ranges.recommendation: [A1] Draft: Eller 2008 sex-specific. Every African source puts the lower limit at ~0.8-1.1 x10^9/L (benign ethnic neutropenia / Duffy-null). Lugada Table 2 column assignment read by position (WBC, neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, eosinophils, basophils) - confirm against the PDF. [A2] Use local limits (Lugada) so healthy Duffy-null children are not flagged as neutropenic; do not substitute Western lower limits (~1.5).

ranges.recommendation: [A3] Default to sex-specific Ugandan (Eller) bands; store method on result. If MedSync labs run enzymatic creatinine, Jaffe-derived intervals may be slightly high - require each lab to declare method and verify. [A4] Creatinine bands must be tagged with method; Jaffe vs enzymatic differences are clinically material at paediatric concentrations. Ugandan labs mostly run Jaffe — prefer method-matched sources (Mekelle compensated Jaffe for adolescents). Kilifi (infants) and Gambia (1–4 y) disagree on the lower limit; report eGFR alongside.

gaps: CD4 absolute (Lugada 2004, all ages): column assignment unverified - read Table 3 in the PDF before signing. Adult CD4 can use Karita 2009 (verified) meanwhile.
Neonates 0-6 days: no haematology interval in any opened source; 7-27 days covered only by Lugada's pooled '<1 year' band. Kumwenda 2012 (Kampala/Malawi infants) has medians only.

Paediatric chemistry: CALIPER main tables not opened (paywall/blocked); Kironde 2013 (Iganga, Uganda, 1-5 y) results table is an image; no African interval after the newborn period for chloride, bicarbonate, GGT or CRP; nothing for 15 days to 1 month.
WHO 2024 anaemia cut-offs for children (6 months to 14 years) not yet loaded; WHO primary PDF not opened (adult values corroborated by a guideline digest).
Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023: diabetes, malaria, TB and syphilis chapters not read (PDF truncated/blocked) - Uganda-specific thresholds unverified.
HIV: Uganda 2022 low-level viraemia definitions only partly readable; the Nov 2024 MoH change of HIV test kits seen only in a May 2025 news report.
Lactate and CRP: only US (Mayo) intervals; no African source.

FBC: no adult interval for IG, RDW-SD, PDW, PCT, P-LCR, P-LCC or 3-part MID/GRAN; MPV and RDW-CV from Eller only (Coulter analyser). DH-615 operator manual not found: HCT measured or calculated, PDW unit and Dymind default ranges unconfirmed.
Adults over ~59 years are not represented in any African source; no sickle-cell-trait source opened.
Thyroid: no paediatric interval (1 month-18 y); no Ugandan interval. PT, APTT and troponin are assay/reagent-specific - the lab must enter its own.
Troponin 99th percentiles were read by text extraction from IFCC task-force papers - check against the current kit insert.
LOINC: 24 of 119 concepts have no code. No LOINC term exists for malaria parasite density in parasites/uL (local code + request to LOINC). Xpert rifampicin resistance has only a TRIAL code (89372-7).
TB: Cepheid Ultra / Uganda NTLP instructions on 'trace' results not opened; number of grades on the current Determine TB-LAM card unconfirmed.
Malaria: which RDT type Uganda procures (HRP2 vs pLDH) and pfhrp2-deletion data not confirmed.
Dipstick grade concentrations come from secondary sources (a reporting form and a CSF study), not the manufacturer IFU.
Blocked during research: PMC/PubMed (browser check), Europe PMC and Springer (rate limits), parts of PLoS and Wiley. A person with library access can close several gaps above quickly.

decisionsForSignOff.question: How does the catalogue hold limits that are not population reference intervals (anaemia cut-offs, glucose and HbA1c diagnostic limits, lipid categories, KDIGO eGFR/ACR stages, viral-load suppression, troponin 99th percentile)?
options: A: everything is a low/high reference band (today's Phase 1 model)
B: range.kind = reference | decision; decision ranges are named category schemes (label, boundary inclusivity, context); each hospital picks a flag basis per concept
decisionsForSignOff.why: ISO 15189 7.3.5 separates biological reference intervals from clinical decision limits. Forcing ATP III or WHO glucose categories into low/high flags produces wrong flags; schemes also let one result show its clinical category.

decisionsForSignOff.question: test.glucose_random and test.glucose_fasting both use obs.glucose, but only fasting glucose has diagnostic limits.
options: B: keep one concept and add a 'context' on the range
decisionsForSignOff.why: Separate LOINC term, separate decision limits (WHO 6.1/7.0 mmol/L), and the NCD feed can trust that a value is fasting.

decisionsForSignOff.question: Troponin I vs T, D-dimer FEU vs DDU, and creatinine by Jaffe vs enzymatic method give numbers that are not interchangeable.
options: A: split concepts (obs.troponin_i_hs, obs.troponin_t_hs; obs.d_dimer as mg/L{FEU} plus obs.d_dimer_ddu) and record creatinine method in the method register
B: one concept each, method in free text
decisionsForSignOff.why: Phase 1 law is one fixed unit and no conversion; a value without its basis cannot be flagged safely. obs.troponin is retired into the split.

decisionsForSignOff.question: HbA1c IFCC (mmol/mol) is an affine conversion that multiplyBy cannot express.
options: A: plain factors only at entry; affine conversions are display-only, computed with IFCC = (NGSP - 2.152) / 0.09148, 0 dp
decisionsForSignOff.why: Keeps the stored value single and canonical (Phase 1); the formula comes from NGSP's master equation.

decisionsForSignOff.question: One FBC test for 5-part (DH-615, 27 parameters) and 3-part (19 parameters) analysers?
options: A: one test.fbc with analyser profiles; MID/GRAN are their own concepts and never map to neutrophils; research-use parameters (NRBC, NLR, PDW-CV...) cannot be released; P-LCR/P-LCC stored but hidden from clinicians
decisionsForSignOff.why: Clinicians order 'FBC', not an analyser; mapping GRAN to neutrophils would silently corrupt the NCD and neutropenia logic.

decisionsForSignOff.question: Accept 62 new concept ids and the reshaping of existing ones (obs.blood_group narrowed to ABO + new obs.rhd_type; obs.malaria_test kept as the shared positive/negative with method detail concepts; 10-pad dipstick adds bilirubin and urobilinogen; obs.troponin retired).
decisionsForSignOff.why: Every existing id is kept; new ids follow the brief's naming.

decisionsForSignOff.question: test.syphilis holds RPR, TPHA, RDT and dual-RDT results; PT/INR has no APTT.
options: A: test.syphilis = treponemal RDT; add test.rpr, test.tpha, test.dual_hiv_syphilis_rdt; add test.coag_screen (PT, INR, APTT)
decisionsForSignOff.why: Each order then has only its own components; the dual RDT's HIV line feeds the national algorithm, never a final HIV status.

decisionsForSignOff.question: Which tests carry a restricted class?
options: hiv: hiv_rapid, hiv_viral_load, cd4, dual HIV/syphilis RDT; tb: tb_xpert, tb_lam, sputum_afb; sexual_reproductive_health: syphilis tests, pregnancy_urine
decisionsForSignOff.why: Uses MedSync's existing restricted classes; CrAg stays unrestricted so cryptococcal results reach the treating team.

decisionsForSignOff.question: HIV testing algorithm and kit names, dipstick brand concentration tables and analyser profiles change over time.
options: A: dated, versioned settings with the kit/lot captured on each test event
decisionsForSignOff.why: Uganda changed HIV kits in Nov 2024; results must stay interpretable under the algorithm that produced them.

decisionsForSignOff.question: Which adult intervals become the drafts?
options: Eller 2008 (Ugandan donors, sex-specific, 2.5-97.5th) with Karita 2009 as cross-check
decisionsForSignOff.recommendation: Eller 2008, verified locally (CLSI EP28: 20 samples, at most 2 outside) on the DH-615 and the chemistry analyser before signing
decisionsForSignOff.why: Ugandan population; numbers spot-checked against the paper. All African studies used other analysers, so local verification is still required.

decisionsForSignOff.question: Flag low Hb on the reference interval (Eller lower limits F 9.8, M 11.6 g/dL) or on WHO 2024 anaemia cut-offs (F 12.0, M 13.0, pregnancy 11.0/10.5/11.0 g/dL) adjusted for altitude (+0.8 g/dL at 1,000-1,499 m, which covers Kampala)?
options: B: WHO 2024 anaemia scheme as the flag basis, adjusted for each facility's elevation; reference interval shown for information
decisionsForSignOff.why: Healthy-donor intervals in a population with iron deficiency put the lower limit far below anaemia: a woman at 10.0 g/dL shows 'in range' under A but has moderate anaemia under WHO. Not flagging anaemia is the larger harm. Needs facility elevation in hospital settings.

decisionsForSignOff.question: Keep African neutrophil lower limits (about 0.9-1.1 x10^9/L)?
decisionsForSignOff.recommendation: Keep, with an interpretive note on Duffy-null-associated neutrophil counts
decisionsForSignOff.why: Duffy-null phenotype is common in people of African ancestry and lowers neutrophil counts without raising infection risk; a higher limit would over-flag healthy people.

decisionsForSignOff.question: How are these interpreted?
options: Fasting glucose by WHO (IFG 6.1-6.9, diabetes >= 7.0 mmol/L); HbA1c >= 6.5 % diabetes; lipids by ATP III categories; random glucose >= 11.1 shown as interpretation only
decisionsForSignOff.recommendation: WHO thresholds (Uganda's guidelines follow WHO; confirm against UCG 2023 when readable)
decisionsForSignOff.why: Healthy-volunteer fasting intervals include undiagnosed diabetes (upper limit 7.3 at 45+), so a reference interval would hide it.

decisionsForSignOff.question: Suppression threshold and categories.
decisionsForSignOff.recommendation: Uganda MoH rule (national programme); add the low-level viraemia band only once the Uganda text is verified
decisionsForSignOff.why: The two disagree exactly at 1000; the national programme governs treatment decisions in Uganda.

decisionsForSignOff.question: Which paediatric haematology bands become drafts?
options: Kilifi (Kenya, CLSI 95%) for 28 days-17 months; Lugada (Uganda, 90%) for 18 months-18 years; nothing for 0-27 days
decisionsForSignOff.recommendation: First option, and do not activate Kilifi's infant platelet lower limits (74-104 x10^9/L)
decisionsForSignOff.why: Lugada uses a 90% interval (flags about 10% of healthy children) and screened only for HIV; Kilifi is CLSI-method. Neonates get 'No reference interval for this age - interpret clinically', never adult ranges.

decisionsForSignOff.question: Reference intervals or WHO immunosuppression cut-offs?
options: Show WHO categories (CD4% by age under 5; CD4 < 200 advanced HIV disease from 5 years) as the decision scheme; keep reference intervals for information
decisionsForSignOff.why: Lugada's CD4% lower limits under 5 years (18.7-18.8 %) sit below WHO's severe cut-off for infants (< 25 %), so a reference flag would miss severe immunosuppression.

decisionsForSignOff.question: Troponin, TSH/FT4/FT3, PT/APTT and D-dimer limits depend on the kit.
options: Lab enters values from its own kit insert per analyser and reagent lot; MedSync ships no default
Use the researched values as defaults
decisionsForSignOff.why: The researched values are for other assays; troponin is sex-specific on some kits.

decisionsForSignOff.question: Where do warfarin INR targets live?
options: On the patient's anticoagulation plan (indication-specific, BCSH/ACCP)
decisionsForSignOff.why: A target depends on the indication, not the test; a lab range cannot know it.

decisionsForSignOff.question: Must each lab declare its creatinine method?
options: Yes: Jaffe or enzymatic, IDMS-traceable; only matching bands apply; eGFR (CKD-EPI 2021) only for adults and only with a declared traceable method
decisionsForSignOff.why: Jaffe reads high in neonates and children; eGFR on a non-traceable method misstages CKD.

decisionsForSignOff.question: Malaria, TB, HIV algorithm, dipstick and RhD reporting.
options: Malaria density in parasites/uL is the main result (plus system hidden, legacy only); Xpert 'trace' stored as its own answer with RIF indeterminate and the WHO trace rule as advice; HIV algorithm in force at go-live chosen and dated; dipstick 'trace' not marked abnormal; weak D reported per transfusion policy
decisionsForSignOff.why: WHO microscopy SOPs do not use the plus system; trace handling depends on HIV status, age and specimen.

decisionsForSignOff.question: What evidence is attached to each signed band?
options: Adults: CLSI EP28 transference check, 20 samples per partition; children: documented transference rationale where local recruitment is not feasible
decisionsForSignOff.why: Matches the Phase 1 signing rule and ISO 15189 7.3.5.

decisions: D1 HbA1c unit conversion: the schema supports only multiplyBy, but NGSP to IFCC is affine. Approve adding a 'formula' field (or an 'offset' field: canonical = other x multiplyBy + offset), implemented as IFCC = (NGSP - 2.152)/0.09148, rounded to 0 dp.

D2 HbA1c thresholds: adopt WHO 2011 >=6.5% for diagnosis. Decide whether to show the ADA prediabetes band 5.7-6.4% (39-47 mmol/mol). Approve an interference caveat (Hb variants, pregnancy, HIV/ART, transfusion, anaemia, dialysis, malaria).

D3 Thyroid: no global default interval. The lab must select its analyser and enter or confirm the interval. Approve the Kenyan DxI and Roche adult intervals as selectable templates, and the ATA fallback (first trimester 0.1-4.0 mU/L) for pregnancy when no lab trimester interval exists.
D4 PT/APTT: reference intervals are lab-entered and versioned per reagent lot (with ISI and MNPT). No shipped defaults.
D5 INR targets live on the patient's anticoagulation plan (indication-based: 2.0-3.0; 2.5-3.5 for mechanical mitral; 3.0-4.0 for recurrent VTE per BCSH), not as a test reference range.

D6 ESR: ship StatPearls step bands (or the Miller age formula if formula limits are supported) flagged as non-local, and commission a local Westergren audit given evidence of higher values in African populations.
D7 Troponin: split hs-cTnT and hs-cTnI concepts (or make the method mandatory). The lab enters its assay's sex-specific 99th percentile. Seed values are not authoritative.

D8 D-dimer: canonical unit 'ug/L FEU'; DDU is a separate unit with no auto-conversion; unit type is mandatory on every result. Age-adjusted cut-off (age x 10 ug/L at >=50 y) only for FEU assays validated for VTE exclusion.

D9 HIV VL: default interpretation follows Uganda MoH 2022 (non-suppressed >=1000 copies/mL), with the WHO 2023 categories (undetectable / <=1000 / >1000) displayed. Resolve the boundary conflict at exactly 1000 copies/mL. Decide whether to show an LLV category (50-999). Support '<LoD'/'not detected' with the assay LoD and specimen type.
D10 HIV log10: calculated only for numeric detected results. Qualified results ('<') are propagated or left blank.
D11 UACR: canonical mg/mmol; mg/g x 0.113 conversion for values. KDIGO A1/A2/A3 boundaries stored per unit as published.

D12 Range schema extensions: approve band keys 'context', 'formula' and 'boundary' (inclusive/exclusive). These are needed for pregnancy bands, indication-based INR targets, age-formula limits (ESR, D-dimer) and WHO vs Uganda VL boundaries.

Combur-10 grades come from a strip-label table reproduced in a CSF study. The Combur-10 urobilinogen, bilirubin and ketone grades were not obtained.
Blood culture: no coded Gram-morphology list or contaminant-comment wording was sourced; these are left as text for Phase 4.
HBsAg/HCV 'invalid' comes from generic RDT control-line rules, not from the WHO hepatitis brief.
LOINC codes were not looked up in this strand (all loinc: null).
existing flags: concept ids for the current 8 dipstick pads were not checked against the live catalogue; reconcile before any addendum.
decisions: Malaria plus system: the recommendation is to record parasites/uL (WHO MM-SOP-09) as the primary result and to keep obs.malaria_plus_grade only as an optional legacy field, hidden by default. The lab lead should confirm whether Ugandan labs still report +/++/+++ (UCG 2023 not readable).

Malaria density: should it be auto-calculated from count and WBC (8000/uL default, patient WBC when available) with the method qualifier stored, or entered directly? The recommendation is to calculate it and allow an override with an audit trail.
Malaria species: a multi-select replaces a separate 'mixed' answer. Should the 'Species not determined' answer be kept?

Malaria RDT: the answer set should follow the kit type (Pf-only HRP2 vs Pf/Pan). Confirm which kits are procured in Uganda and whether the kit type is held at test-definition level or recorded per run.

Xpert trace: record 'MTB detected trace' as its own answer with RIF 'indeterminate', never converted to positive or negative. Show the WHO interpretation (PLHIV, children, extrapulmonary = positive; adults with TB in the previous 5 years = culture) as decision support. The lab lead or TB focal person should confirm the Uganda NTLP rule.

HIV algorithm: which algorithm is in force at go-live (2022 Determine/Stat-Pak/SD Bioline, or the Nov 2024 Wondfo/One Step/MeriScreen)? The recommendation is versioned algorithm configuration with effective dates, and kit name and lot captured per test.

Urinalysis: (a) is trace protein or trace leucocytes flagged abnormal? The sources say small/1+ or greater is significant, so trace is currently set to not abnormal. (b) Is trace blood split into haemolysed and non-haemolysed? (c) Should approximate concentrations be held per strip brand?
CrAg titre: the opened IMMY procedure starts at 1:5, not 1:2. Should the titre be stored as a coded ordinal (proposed), as a reciprocal integer, or both (for trending)?
RPR titre: coded ordinal (1:1-1:128, extensible) or reciprocal integer?

RhD weak D: genotyping is rarely available. Should 'weak D' be reportable at all, or should such patients be reported and managed as RhD negative for transfusion and anti-D in pregnancy? This needs blood bank sign-off (Phase 4).
Urine hCG positive is set abnormal=false. Confirm.
Syphilis: should test.syphilis be split into separate orderable tests (RPR, TPHA/TPPA, syphilis RDT, dual HIV/syphilis RDT)?
TB LAM: the equivocal answer is kept non-abnormal and prompts a repeat. Confirm.

gaps.issue: No LOINC code for Plasmodium (falciparum or sp) parasites per microlitre [#/volume] by microscopy was found. Checked loinc.org group LG41640-0 (Plasmodium), VSAC value set 2.16.840.1.113762.1.4.1146.466 and web search. Available quantitative codes are % parasitaemia only (101996-7 Pf; 53556-7 Plasmodium sp) and 48427-9 per 1000 RBC (in VSAC list, not opened).
gaps.suggestion: Keep a local code for parasites/uL (thick film) and request a new term from LOINC (loinc.org/submissions); meanwhile also send the 51587-4 presence result.

gaps.issue: No P. falciparum-specific [Presence] by light microscopy code exists; only genus-level 51587-4 plus species identifier 32206-5.
Rapid CrAg codes found only for Serum (70910-5) and CSF (70911-3); no Ser/Plas/Bld rapid code located.
gaps.suggestion: Use 70910-5 for serum/plasma; flag fingerstick whole-blood CrAg as a gap if used.

gaps.issue: Only a TRIAL-status code (89372-7) is available; the earlier NAA code 48176-2 is DEPRECATED.
gaps.suggestion: Use 89372-7 and re-check status at each LOINC release.

gaps.issue: Only PDW in fL (32207-3) verified; analysers that report PDW as % have no verified code in this pass.
gaps.suggestion: Confirm the analyser's PDW unit before mapping.

gaps.issue: NLM Clinical Tables API (clinicaltables.nlm.nih.gov) was blocked by the proxy (HTTP 403 via curl; HTTP 429 via WebFetch). All verification was done one-by-one on loinc.org term pages (LOINC 2.82).
gaps.suggestion: Bulk-check against the LOINC release table (Loinc.csv) once downloaded with a free LOINC account.

options: 788-0 Erythrocyte [DistWidth] in Blood by Automated count (CBC panel member, widely used)
115741-1 Erythrocytes [DistWidth] in Red Blood Cells by Coefficient of variation (new, explicit, pairs with 115742-9 RDW-SD)
decisions.recommendation: 115741-1 for RDW-CV so CV and SD use one matched pair, since 21000-5 (RDW-SD) is deprecated. Use 788-0 instead if receivers expect the CBC panel's own member.

options: Mass 1975-2 / 1968-7 (mg/dL), which are the hepatic-panel members
decisions.recommendation: SI codes, matching Ugandan lab reporting; confirm the unit each site's analyser emits.
Map by what the analyser actually measures. Most serum chemistry analysers report total CO2, so use 2028-9; use 1963-8 for blood-gas-calculated HCO3.
Bind by specimen. ED/resus POC lactate goes to 32693-4.
If results are captured as neg/trace/+/++/+++, the ordinal presence codes fit better. If captured as mg/dL steps, use the mass codes. Pick one rule and apply it to every pad.

decisions.topic: Rapid vs laboratory immunoassay codes (HBsAg, HCV Ab, syphilis, HIV)
decisions.recommendation: Bind by method. Default to the rapid codes for facility-level RDTs and switch to the IA codes when ELISA/CLIA is used.
38379-4 for detection. 89372-7 (TRIAL) for rif resistance, as there is no active option.

options: Send SI child codes under the panel codes (24325-3, 24331-1, 24320-4)
Send panel children as the listed mass codes
decisions.recommendation: Keep SI child codes. The panels list mass/BUN members, so tell exchange partners (e.g. DHIS2/CPHL/national LIS) that panel children are SI equivalents. For UEC, consider a local order code rather than 24320-4/24362-6, because Ugandan urea is not BUN.

options: Store % and IFCC mmol/mol (59261-8) as separate observations
decisions.recommendation: Store both when the analyser emits both. Note that the 59261-8 long name now reads '...standardized per IFCC-RMP for CDT...'; it is still the IFCC HbA1c term according to its description.
PPP codes for lab coagulation; 34714-6 only for fingerstick POC INR.
